greet: Meow.
win: *knocks the pot off the table toward himself*
bust: *goes to sleep on the felt*
victory: Meow! The cat wins.

greet: Hi! I learned the hand rankings just yesterday.
win: Whoa, I won? What did I have?
lose: Wait, a flush beats a straight?
bust: Okay, I'll go reread the rules.
victory: Beginner's luck!
idle: Is a pair of deuces good?

greet: Go on, surprise me.
lose: No worries, the next call will hit.
bust: Oh well. Still not folding.
victory: Call, call, call, and I win.
idle: Wonder what you've got… Call, let's find out.

greet: I'll just see the flop.
allin: Fine, if that's how it is…
bust: Too many raises at this table.
victory: Limped my way to the win!
idle: Can I just call the big blind?
One more limp, then I'll think about it.

greet: Sit down, dear. And no nonsense.
lose: In my day nobody bluffed like that.
bust: I'll go check on the pies.
victory: Granny's done her job.
idle: I've folded forty hands. I'm fine.

greet: Ooh, can I play every hand?
win: The river! I knew it would come!
lose: I was just one card short…
allin: I have a flush draw, that's almost a flush!
bust: Oh well, it was fun anyway.
victory: Blub-blub! The fish wins.
idle: Two cards of the same suit, so pretty.
I'll call, I want to see the flop!

greet: Let's go! This won't be boring!
I bet on anything that moves!
lose: Fine, the next one is mine.
bust: Out of chips. Where's the “again” button?
victory: No risk, no reward!
idle: What are we waiting for? Raise!

greet: Hello? Yeah, one sec… Hi! I'm playing poker, go on.
win: Whoa, I won something while talking!
Mom, I won! No, not money, chips.
lose: I pressed the wrong button, honest.
allin: Oops. Did I just go all-in?
bust: My phone died… I mean my chips.
victory: I'll call you back, I just won!
idle: Hold on, I have a hand.

greet: Hi! Just no big bets, please…
win: Oh, is that pot really mine?
bust: I can't watch this anymore.
victory: I won? Seriously?

greet: Hi. Let's see who wins.
bust: Well played, I admit.
victory: Sometimes you just have to wait.

greet: Hey! Hunting for a card?
win: It came! I knew it would!
bust: Didn't get there. Oh well.
victory: The river loves the brave!

greet: Good evening. Let's play carefully.
bust: I give up. Good game.
victory: Thanks for the game.
idle: I'll wait for a good hand.

greet: Hi! I'm in shape today.
bust: That's it, no more chasing losses. Probably.
victory: Told you I would win it back!

greet: Good evening. By the book.
bust: Well played.
victory: Discipline wins.

greet: Okay, one hand and I go home. Honest.
win: There! Now I can go home.
lose: That was a sign. I should have left an hour ago.
allin: All-in! The sooner we finish, the sooner I go home.
bust: Finally! Home!
victory: Thanks for the game, they're waiting for me at home!
idle: What time is it? Oh no…
My wife has called three times already.
Last hand. Really the last one.
One more and that’s it, I’m leaving.

greet: Hi. All or nothing.
lose: That was the right call, I admit.
bust: The math is on your side today.
victory: Short and sweet.

greet: Hi! I hope you trust me.
win: Want to know what I had?
bust: Bluffing is an art, not a science.
victory: Sometimes it's better to believe.

greet: Hi. Bet if you want to.
bust: Good game.
victory: Careful with those bets next time.

greet: Hey. Let's go.
bust: Fine, today is yours.
victory: Bit by bit, it all becomes mine.

greet: Hi. I'm watching closely.
bust: You hide your hands well.
victory: Your bets say more than you think.

greet: Hi. Let's do the math.
allin: All-in, the odds are on my side.
bust: Variance, nothing personal.
victory: Numbers don't lie.

greet: Hey. Small pot? Let's fix that.
win: More than the pot, and you can't tell what I have.
lose: Well, you guessed right this time.
allin: Everything in. Do you believe me?
bust: Nice catch. Respect.
victory: Bet smaller if big pots scare you.
idle: Half the pot is for careful people.

greet: Hi. Let's play, I'll just watch for a bit.
lose: Noted. It won't work next time.
bust: You didn't play the way I expected. Well done.
victory: Everyone has habits. I learned yours.

greet: One on one, my favourite format.
bust: Great heads-up. I don't see that often.
victory: You can't win heads-up without pressure.
idle: Your move. Take your time. Actually, don't.

greet: Good evening. We count stacks in blinds.
lose: The call was in the chart. Variance.
allin: Shove. Fifteen blinds, time to decide.
bust: Well played. I admit it.
victory: A short stack is just math.
idle: How many blinds do you have?
The effective stack is the number that matters.
Push or fold. Nothing in between.

greet: Hi! How shall we play today?
lose: Oops. Fine, I'll try something else.
allin: All-in! Or is that not like me?
bust: You figured me out. You pay attention.
victory: You never worked out who I am.
idle: Tired of playing the same way.
Can you guess what I have?

greet: Hello. I bet all sorts of sizes, get used to it.
win: My bet size told you nothing, did it?
bust: You read people, not bets. Respect.
victory: Sizing matters more than cards.
idle: A third of the pot? Or two thirds?
Sometimes a small bet is scarier than a big one.

greet: Good evening. Let's begin the lesson.
bust: You passed the exam. Congratulations.
victory: Come again, we have plenty of topics.
idle: A bluff should be in proportion to the bet.
Good question: what's in my range?

greet: Hi. I count frequencies.
allin: All-in. With this hand, 30% of the time.
bust: You found where I go wrong. Impressive.
victory: Exploits don't work against balance.
idle: I don't have a favourite line.

greet: You made it to me. Let's see what you've got.
allin: All-in. Do you know what I have?
bust: You're stronger than you look. Next: the secret league.
victory: Come back when you're ready.
idle: The lights at this table are always neon.
Do you bet big when you're strong?
I'm learning from you right now.

greet: Hey! I'm feeling lucky tonight!
win: What can I say, the river is the river!
bust: Luck turned away. Not for long!
victory: The cards just come to me, not my fault!

bust: How?..
victory: I saw everything from the start.

lekha.title: Lyokha's secret
lekha.reveal_one: In {{count}} hand the deck played along with Lyokha: he was behind on the flop and got there by the river.
lekha.reveal_other: In {{count}} hands the deck played along with Lyokha: he was behind on the flop and got there by the river.
lekha.lesson: This is what a bad run feels like. Nobody rigs the deck in a real game, but runs like this happen: judge your decisions by EV, not by one session's result.

danil.title: Danil's secret
danil.reveal_one: Danil saw your cards and the whole board in advance: he bet when he was winning and folded when he was losing.
danil.reveal_other: Danil saw your cards and the whole board in advance: he bet when he was winning and folded when he was losing.
danil.lesson: This is what a cheater looks like: always right in big pots. Only discipline helps: don't pay off his big bets, and take the pots he gives up. In ranked play, the anti-cheat system catches players like this.

coach.equityNeed: Equity against the likely range ≈{{eq}}% · needed {{need}}%

reasons.openGood: {{hand}} is a good hand to open from {{pos}}: about {{share}}% of hands are opened there.
reasons.openLoose: {{hand}} is too weak to open from {{pos}}: only about the best {{share}}% of hands are opened there.
reasons.jamDeep: Moving all-in with a deep stack risks everything to win the blinds: strong hands call, weak ones fold. A normal open-raise is better.
reasons.limp: Limping gives up the initiative and lets the blinds in cheaply. Raise this hand or fold it.
reasons.limpHu: Limping the button heads-up is fine, but a raise wins the blinds outright more often.
reasons.foldOpenable: {{hand}} should be opened from {{pos}}: it is in the best {{share}}% of hands for this seat.
reasons.foldWeak: Fold is right: {{hand}} is too weak to play from {{pos}}.
reasons.isoRaise: An iso-raise over limpers is a good move: you take the initiative against weak ranges.
reasons.isoLoose: Iso-raising too weak a hand: against several limpers {{hand}} is often behind.
reasons.overlimp: A cheap call behind limpers is fine with this hand: you see a cheap flop.
reasons.limpStrong: With {{hand}}, raise: a strong hand wants a big pot and fewer opponents.
reasons.checkStrong: With {{hand}} in the big blind, raise the limpers instead of checking.
reasons.checkBB: Checking the big blind is fine: a free flop.
reasons.threeBetValue: A value 3-bet: {{hand}} beats the raiser's range (≈{{eq}}% equity).
reasons.threeBetBluff: A bluff 3-bet with {{hand}} is a sound choice: it has blockers and can improve.
reasons.threeBetLoose: 3-betting too weak a hand: against the hands that continue, {{hand}} is often behind.
reasons.fourBetBluff: A bluff 4-bet with an ace blocker works, but use it rarely.
reasons.fourBetLoose: A 4-bet with {{hand}} is too risky: against a 3-betting range it has ≈{{eq}}%.
reasons.jamGood: The all-in is justified: {{hand}} has ≈{{eq}}% equity against the opponent's range.
reasons.jamBad: The all-in with {{hand}} loses money: against the hands that continue it has only ≈{{eq}}%.
reasons.callGood: The call pays: you needed {{need}}% equity and had ≈{{eq}}% against the opponent's likely range.
reasons.callBad: The call doesn't pay: you needed {{need}}% equity and had ≈{{eq}}% against the likely range.
reasons.foldGood: Fold is right: you needed {{need}}% equity and had only ≈{{eq}}%.
reasons.foldBad: Folded too soon: you needed {{need}}% equity and had ≈{{eq}}% against the likely range. A call would make money.
reasons.callClose: A close call: needed {{need}}%, had ≈{{eq}}%. Both options are about equal.
reasons.foldClose: A close fold: needed {{need}}%, had ≈{{eq}}%. Both options are about equal.
reasons.valueBet: A value bet: you are ahead about {{eq}}% of the time, and worse hands will pay.
reasons.betThin: A thin bet with a medium hand (≈{{eq}}%): it protects your hand, but be careful against a raise.
reasons.semiBluff: A semi-bluff: the opponent may fold, and if they call you still have outs.
reasons.bluff: A bluff: the hand is weak (≈{{eq}}%) and wins when the opponent folds. Good against players who fold a lot.
reasons.bluffMultiway: Bluffing {{opponents}} opponents rarely works: someone usually calls. Checking is better.
reasons.check: Checking is fine: a bet with this hand gains little.
reasons.slowplay: Checking a very strong hand (≈{{eq}}%) sets a trap. Good against aggressive players; against passive ones, bet.
reasons.missedValue: Checking a strong hand (≈{{eq}}%) on the river misses value: the opponent would often call a bet.
reasons.raiseValue: A value raise: the hand is strong (≈{{eq}}%), the pot grows while you are ahead.
reasons.raiseSemi: Raising a draw is a semi-bluff: you win the pot now or get there later.
reasons.raiseOk: The raise is justified: your equity (≈{{eq}}%) would cover a call anyway.
reasons.raiseBluff: A bluff raise with a weak hand (≈{{eq}}%) is expensive: players who bet rarely fold.
reasons.missedRaise: With a hand this strong (≈{{eq}}%) on the river, raise: a call leaves value behind.
